extracted.intended_audience: grant writers and proposal developers (especially in human services/social service agencies); first-time and experienced nonprofit program staff seeking guidance on grantsmanship
extracted.subtask_description: Practical, chapter-by-chapter guidance for planning, writing, budgeting, and submitting grant proposals in the human services/social services sector, including needs assessment, program design, evaluation, and agency documentation. Geared to both first-time and organizational grant writers.

rubrics_metrics.name: An orientation to proposal writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Overview of proposal writing and the field of grantsmanship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter likely frames purpose, basic concepts, and what successful proposal writing entails; detailed content not present on this page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Key terms and definitions related to proposal writing and grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General definitional guidance appears as a chapter heading; specific definitions are in the book text (not on this page).

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of grant applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Different categories and formats of grant applications a writer may encounter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter likely describes distinctions between program, project, operating, capital, foundation, government, and other application types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Components of a proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: The standard sections and elements that make up a grant proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TOC lists this as a discrete chapter; specifics (e.g., needs statement, goals, budget) are elaborated elsewhere in the book.

rubrics_metrics.name: The process of submitting a proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural steps from finalizing the application to submission and follow-up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes submission timelines, required forms, packaging, and logistics; detailed instructions are in the chapter itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: The difference between grants and contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguishes grants from contracts in scope, expectations, and legal/administrative implications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter likely explains differences in deliverables, reporting, funding terms, and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizing the writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods for structuring and managing the proposal writing process and document organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers outlines, assignment of writing tasks, version control, and logical flow of the proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing for an established organization or a new organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Adaptation of proposal content and tone depending on whether the applicant is an established agency or a start-up/new organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on emphasizing track record, capacity, or potential; tailoring agency capability statements accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing style and format
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidelines on prose style, clarity, readability, and formatting conventions for proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Likely covers plain language, active voice, conciseness, headings, fonts, pagination, and following funder format rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using technology in proposal development
rubrics_metrics.description: How to employ technology tools to support proposal research, writing, collaboration, and submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May include software for word processing, collaboration platforms, budgeting tools, and document management.

rubrics_metrics.name: The role and use of search engines
rubrics_metrics.description: Strategies for using search engines effectively to locate funders, data, and relevant program information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers search techniques, query formulation, and evaluating the credibility of online sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of funder's web sites
rubrics_metrics.description: How to analyze and extract relevant requirements, priorities, and guidance from funder websites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes reading funder instructions, priorities, past awards, and FAQ pages to align proposals with funder expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluating data and other information
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessing the quality, relevance, and credibility of data used to justify needs and program design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes source evaluation, appropriate use of statistics, and integrating evidence into the needs statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic submission of the proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements and best practices for submitting proposals electronically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers file formats, system checks, attachments, deadlines, and confirmation/receipt practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding the agency, the community, and the funder
rubrics_metrics.description: Three-part analysis to align proposals with internal capacity, community need, and funder priorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serves as an umbrella for the subsequent focused chapters on agency, community, and funder understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding the agency
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessing organizational mission, capacity, staffing, and past performance to demonstrate capability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Informs agency capability statements and how to present strengths and limitations to funders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding the community
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyzing community characteristics, needs, demographics, and assets relevant to the proposed program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Feeds into the needs/problem statement and program design; see related chapters on community data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding the funder
rubrics_metrics.description: Researching funder mission, priorities, funding history, eligibility rules, and application expectations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key to tailoring proposals and identifying fit; includes reading RFPs and funder guidance carefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem- or needs-based program development
rubrics_metrics.description: Developing programs that respond directly to identified problems or community needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes linking needs analysis to program goals, objectives, and interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding the community through data
rubrics_metrics.description: Using quantitative and qualitative data to create a rigorous picture of local needs and conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes data sources, interpretation, and how to present data persuasively in the proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding barriers to service
rubrics_metrics.description: Identifying obstacles community members face in accessing services and how the proposed program addresses them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps design realistic interventions and justify program approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program design and theoretical orientations
rubrics_metrics.description: Grounding program activities in theoretical frameworks and evidence-based approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses selecting appropriate models, logic models, and linking theory to practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conceptualizing program ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: Transforming needs and theory into concrete program concepts and interventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers brainstorming, feasibility assessment, and specifying target populations and services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Working with a collaborative
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on partnering with other organizations, roles/responsibilities, and presenting collaborations to funders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses memoranda of understanding, coordination, and how to show collaborative capacity and added value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sustainability and institutionalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Planning for program continuation, scaling, and embedding within organizational structures beyond grant funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers revenue diversification, policy integration, and strategies to demonstrate long-term viability to funders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing the needs or problem statement
rubrics_metrics.description: How to craft a clear, evidence-based statement that defines the problem the proposal will address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This and subsequent related chapters provide step-by-step guidance on composing an effective needs statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions (needs/problem statement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific definitions relevant to needs/problem statements (separate chapter instance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies terms used in that section of the book; details are in-text.

rubrics_metrics.name: The purpose of the needs/problem statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Explains why the needs statement matters and what it should accomplish in the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Likely emphasizes establishing urgency, evidence of need, and the gap the program will fill.

rubrics_metrics.name: A guide to writing the needs/problem statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Stepwise advice and criteria for developing a persuasive needs statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May include structure, use of data, linking to funder priorities, and common pitfalls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing goals, objectives, and the implementation plan
rubrics_metrics.description: How to state goals and measurable objectives and to outline concrete implementation steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Connects high-level aims to specific, measurable, achievable, relevant, time-bound (SMART) objectives and activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section one : goals and objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed treatment of formulating program goals and measurable objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers scope, level of ambition, indicators, and aligning objectives with evaluation measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section two : implementation plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed guidance on describing program activities, timelines, staff roles, and operational logistics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes sequencing of activities, staffing plans, and delivery mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing the evaluation plan
rubrics_metrics.description: How to design an evaluation that measures program effectiveness and supports accountability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes choosing outcomes, measures, data collection methods, and reporting plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: The benefits of evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Rationale for including evaluation: program improvement, accountability, and evidence building.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains how evaluation strengthens proposals and program practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Developing an evaluation plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical steps to create an evaluation framework aligned with objectives and resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers formative vs. summative evaluation, logic models, and evaluation budgeting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing the evaluation section
rubrics_metrics.description: Presentation tips for the evaluation portion of the proposal, including level of detail and clarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses what reviewers expect to see and how to demonstrate credible measurement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other evaluation considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional issues such as ethical concerns, feasibility, and external evaluators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May discuss limitations, data access, and how to handle challenging evaluation contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creating the budget
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles and steps for developing a realistic, funder-compliant budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes cost estimation, allowable/unallowable costs, and linking budget items to activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of budgets
rubrics_metrics.description: Different budget formats and types (e.g., line-item, program, categorical, indirect costs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps writers choose the appropriate budget structure for the funder and project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budgeting for the first-time grant writer
rubrics_metrics.description: Special guidance for newcomers on estimating costs and presenting a credible budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers practical tips, common mistakes, and conservative cost estimation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other budgeting issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional budget topics such as match requirements, in-kind contributions, and budget justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses negotiation, flexibility, and funder-specific budget rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency capability and finishing touches
rubrics_metrics.description: How to present organizational capacity and finalize the proposal for submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes editing, proofreading, consistency checks, and assembling attachments.

rubrics_metrics.name: The agency capability statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific guidance on composing a statement that demonstrates an agency's ability to carry out the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers history, staffing, past performance, governance, and fiscal controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requesting letters of support
rubrics_metrics.description: How to solicit and structure persuasive letters of support and partnership endorsements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes who to ask, timing, and what content to request to strengthen the proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: The proposal abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on writing a concise summary of the proposal's purpose, methods, and expected outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers length, emphasis, and how to craft an effective executive summary.

rubrics_metrics.name: The title and title page
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructions on selecting a clear title and completing required title page information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes consistency with funder requirements and presenting key proposal identifiers.

rubrics_metrics.name: The cover letter
rubrics_metrics.description: How to draft a professional cover letter to accompany a proposal submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers tone, key points to include, and signature/authority conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frequently asked questions (FAQs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Answers to common practical questions about proposal writing and submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides troubleshooting and clarifications for common uncertainties faced by grant writers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix A: Estimating time
rubrics_metrics.description: Tools and guidance for estimating staff time and project timelines required for proposal and project implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps budget time realistically for proposal development and program delivery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix B: Funding resource information
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists and descriptions of funding sources and resources useful to grant seekers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides curated leads for further funder research and potential grant opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: References and suggested readings
rubrics_metrics.description: Bibliographic materials and further reading to support proposal writing and grantsmanship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for deeper study and sourcing evidence for proposals.
